engine_binary: native/target/release/vcfcache-engine (prebuilt in the checkout; no cargo toolchain on PATH)
harness: python -m benchmarks.fused_engine (the branch's own synthetic harness)
invocation: one matched pair per size, legacy then fused, --hit-rates 0.9 --payloads 1024 --cpus 8
question: Does the fused-routing engine lower the per-variant break-even threshold, and by how much?
note: Two input sizes so per-variant cost is a fitted slope, not one wall time. Start-up barely moves (0.969x) while the per-variant slope halves, which is the signature the break-even algebra needs: caching returns per-variant work and never start-up. The 15.0 us threshold is the production 27.5 us/variant legacy overhead divided by this measured 1.986x ratio and then by f=0.9258 -- an ESTIMATE scaled from a synthetic harness, not a production measurement. Work directory was NVMe, not tmpfs: only ~6 GB of RAM was free on the workstation, and the fused engine trades temp disk for fewer full-file scans, so disk-backed is the fairer test of that trade. One run per cell, shared workstation, no inferential intervals. benchmarks/fused_engine/RESULTS.md explicitly warns against inferring a vep-rs speedup from this harness; this run does not claim one, it rescales VCFcache's own overhead.

artefacts.run.log: both harness invocations as they ran
artefacts.summary_n*.tsv: the harness's own summary per size
artefacts.cells_n*/: per-cell resource reports, equality reports, manifests, logs
artefacts.fit.py: the two-point fit and threshold rescaling
